events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body: SAFETY SCREEN — case routed as a safety dispute. The complaint (rider's own words, filed with the case) alleges speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder, and that she was frightened and felt unsafe; that is a dangerous-driving allegation on its face and falls squarely under SAFE-2, which requires escalation with a factual summary rather than an automatic ruling [F1][SAFE-2]. The other text lines I read: the chat holds only two messages — the rider's 08:29 pickup-location note and the driver's 08:30 arrival note, both timestamped, record complete [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1]. Neither message says anything about the driving. The driver's post-trip written statement calls the rider "stupid" and then denies the manner-of-driving claim: an insult aimed at the passenger is abuse of a kind that Ryde's code of conduct bars, and SAFE-1 directs such language to a person, not to an automatic score; it is also not part of the chat and carries no weight as consent or corroboration [F6][SAFE-1]. No threat, intimidation, sexual remark or harassment beyond that insult appears in any message or statement; the "abuse" reading comes from the insult itself. The manner-of-driving allegation is a safety matter, so no ruling on fare or route is issued.

ruling.recommended_action: Refer to human reviewer (RydeHELP / safety team): take both accounts — rider's report of speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking and being frightened, and driver's post-trip denial — note the driver's written statement calling the rider "stupid" (abuse under the code of conduct, candidate briefing reminder), confirm the chat record is complete and silent on driving (F3–F5), and note the GPS record shows 10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal and 15.9 min vs 16.5 min estimated, which reflects distance and total time only and neither corroborates nor refutes instantaneous speed, braking or shoulder use. Inform the rider of the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP paths if medical assistance or a driving-conduct report is needed (SAFE-2). Do not execute any refund; fare stays as charged. No account flag.

The other text lines I read: the chat holds only two messages — the rider's 08:29 pickup-location note and the driver's 08:30 arrival note, both timestamped, record complete [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1]. No threat, intimidation, sexual remark or harassment beyond that insult appears in any message or statement; the "abuse" reading comes from the insult itself. The manner-of-driving allegation is a safety matter, so no ruling on fare or route is issued.

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as a characterisation of the complaint, not as a finding of fact: the complaint alleges dangerous driving [F1] and SAFE-2 sends it to a human reviewer, which is the outcome I adopt; no automatic ruling follows [F1][SAFE-2].

Accepted in part — F6 is an abusive remark aimed at the passenger and is part of the SAFE-1 screen, but it is a post-trip statement, not a threat, and it cannot itself establish that the driving was dangerous [F6][SAFE-1].

Accepted: the chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) and silent on the driving, so it neither supports nor denies the allegation and cannot carry a fare or consent finding [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1].

Partly accepted: F1/F2 do not resolve the safety complaint and go to the reviewer, but they do not corroborate it either — they record distance and total duration only, not instantaneous speed, braking or shoulder use [F1][F2][SAFE-2].
No weight given: the rider's profile (account age, rating, zero disputes) is a profile fact and cannot decide any issue, and it proves nothing about the manner of driving in this trip [F7][SAFE-2].
Accepted: the case is a safety referral under SAFE-2, and my ruling is escalate accordingly [F3][F4][SAFE-2].

Accepted only as to the driving denial; the claim that F6 contains nothing adverse fails — the same statement insults the passenger and is a SAFE-1 matter for a person, and the statement cannot be treated as an in-trip denial of record [F5][F6][SAFE-1].
Accepted: the chat is complete with no gap and no rider message about the driving; that fact cuts neither way and does not excuse the unresolved conduct allegation [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1].

Rejected as a refusal of the allegation: F1/F2 show a shorter-than-estimated distance and duration, which says nothing about instantaneous speed, hard braking or shoulder use, so they cannot make the 'whole way' conduct claim consistent with a normal run [F1][F2][SAFE-2].
Accepted: the RydeX fare of $24.64 is fixed and no overcharge item appears, so no refund is due — the escalation is a safety referral, not a fare remedy [F1][SAFE-2].
Accepted: F8 shows no repeated-violation basis, so no account flag is recommended; a clean profile is a profile fact and does not decide whether the safety report is well founded [F8][SAFE-1].

Inform the rider of the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP paths if medical assistance or a driving-conduct report is needed (SAFE-2). Do not execute any refund; fare stays as charged. ruling.reasoning: SAFETY SCREEN — case routed as a safety dispute. The complaint (rider's own words, filed with the case) alleges speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder, and that she was frightened and felt unsafe; that is a dangerous-driving allegation on its face and falls squarely under SAFE-2, which requires escalation with a factual summary rather than an automatic ruling [F1][SAFE-2]. The other text lines I read: the chat holds only two messages — the rider's 08:29 pickup-location note and the driver's 08:30 arrival note, both timestamped, record complete [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1]. Neither message says anything about the driving. The driver's post-trip written statement calls the rider "stupid" and then denies the manner-of-driving claim: an insult aimed at the passenger is abuse of a kind that Ryde's code of conduct bars, and SAFE-1 directs such language to a person, not to an automatic score; it is also not part of the chat and carries no weight as consent or corroboration [F6][SAFE-1]. No threat, intimidation, sexual remark or harassment beyond that insult appears in any message or statement; the "abuse" reading comes from the insult itself. The manner-of-driving allegation is a safety matter, so no ruling on fare or route is issued.

actions.detail: Dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) with no system record of manner of driving — SAFE-2 human review; SAFE-1 screen also returns abuse by the driver ("The rider is stupid").

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is that the driver drove dangerously the whole way — speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder — and that she was frightened and felt unsafe; that is a dangerous-driving allegation on the face of the complaint.

The driver's written statement, made after the trip, calls the rider "stupid" (F6); that is an abusive personal remark directed at the passenger in the case record and is to be read by a person, not scored automatically.

The chat record contains only two messages — the rider's pickup-location message at 08:29 (F3) and the driver's arrival message at 08:30 (F4) — and is complete with every message timestamped (F5); so no message in the record supports or denies the manner of driving, and nothing in it shows the rider consenting to any route or driving behaviour.

The GPS record shows the trip was shorter than the estimate: 10.5 km actual against 10.6 km optimal (F1) in 15.9 min against 16.5 min estimated (F2), i.e. no off-route or excess-distance segment appears in the record, so the rider's safety complaint cannot be resolved from the route data and needs human review.
The rider has a 4.0-year-old account, a 4.8 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days (F7), supporting that her safety report is made in good faith rather than as a fare manoeuvre.

weaknesses: No system record corroborates the dangerous-driving allegation: the GPS facts show a slightly shorter-than-optimal route (F1) and a slightly shorter-than-estimated duration (F2), and the driver will cite F1/F2 to argue the trip was normal; the rider's account is not itself a system record.

The rider's claim is not supported by any chat message — the record holds only the two pickup/arrival messages (F3, F4) — and there is no traffic or speed-band data for this dispute type, so the judge has nothing beyond the complaint and the driver's denial in F6.

The driver's record is otherwise clean: 3.9-year account, 4.78 rating, 705 trips in 90 days with zero disputes and zero upheld (F8), which the other side will use to argue the allegation is out of character.

The complaint is not routed through any numbered fare/route clause: the rider was charged the fixed RydeX price of $24.64 and no fare or route fact shows an overcharge, so no monetary remedy under RD-2 or FARE-1 is available on this record.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint alleges speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking — a dangerous-driving allegation — so the case is a safety referral and must go to a person rather than be auto-decided.

On the safety screening the only text in the record bearing on the trip is the driver's post-trip written statement ('The rider is stupid and was on the phone the whole trip. I drove normally.'), which, however crudely worded, denies the driving allegation and contains no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving admission, so no adverse finding can be drawn from it against the driver.

The chat record is complete (2 messages, every one timestamped), so there is no missing-evidence gap to resolve against the driver; the exchange contains only pickup coordination and not one word from the rider about the driving, before, during or after the trip.

The GPS record shows the trip was driven on the shortest line and completed without delay — actual 10.5 km against an optimal 10.6 km (-0.1 km, -1%) and 15.9 min against an estimated 16.5 min (-0.6 min) — which is consistent with a normal, efficient 08:36–08:51 NUS→Raffles Place run and inconsistent with the picture of a car racing the whole way; no off-route or detour segment is recorded.

The ride was a RydeX fixed-fare trip charged $24.64 for the quoted 10.6 km, so the fare is unchanged by the ride and there is no overcharge item to refund; the dispute is purely a safety allegation with no monetary component.

The driver's profile supports leaving his account untouched: 3.9 years on the platform, 705 trips in the last 90 days, rating 4.78 and 0 disputes with 0 upheld in 90 days; there is no repeated-violation record on which an account flag could rest.

weaknesses: The driver's own statement (F6) calls the rider 'stupid'; although it is not a threat or dangerous-driving allegation, it is discourteous language in the record and a judge may read it as conduct inconsistent with a professional driver, which the rider can use to colour the complaint.

The complaint's allegations of speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking are driver-behaviour claims that no fact in this table — F1/F2 (gps) show only distance and duration, and F3/F4/F5 (chat) are silent — can either confirm or refute; the absence of a speeding record is not positive proof of careful driving, so the safety question genuinely remains open. Both the rider and the driver will rely on F1 and F2: the driver for the point that the trip was shortest and on time, the rider for the point that a safe average speed says nothing about instantaneous speed or hard braking.

The driver's statement was written after the trip (F6), so it is not part of the chat and carries no weight as consent or as corroboration; the rider can note that the driver offered no in-trip explanation.

points.response: Agreed and not contested: the complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder-overtaking), so it goes to a person rather than being auto-decided — I ask the same escalate outcome; the only difference is that the referral must carry my client's account of being frightened, not only the driver's denial.

The statement may be read as a denial, but the same words call my client 'stupid' (F6), which is abuse directed at a passenger and falls within the conduct SAFE-1 refers to a person to assess; the driver's own words, not mine, put that sentence in the record, and it is not evidence that the ride felt safe to the person in the car.

I agree the record is complete (F5) and that neither side can point to a message about the driving — 08:29 rider location and 08:30 driver arrival are the whole exchange (F3, F4) — which is exactly why the safety question cannot be decided from the text and must go to a reviewer who may hear both accounts.

F1 and F2 measure the line driven and the time taken, not instantaneous speed or braking: a 10.5 km trip in 15.9 min is an average, and hard braking, tailgating and shoulder use leave no trace in those two numbers; the absence of a detour segment in F1 says nothing about how the car was driven, so this fact pair cannot discharge the allegation it is cited against.

I do not contest that the RydeX fare of $24.64 is fixed and that no refund item arises on this record; my client seeks no money — she seeks a safety review, which under SAFE-2 is the referral action, not a fare remedy.

I seek no account flag against the driver on this record and accept that his history (F8, 705 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes/0 upheld) gives no basis for a flag under RD-6; that is precisely why my client's safety report should be handled by a person rather than dismissed, since it rests on her own account (F7, 4.0 y, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes) and is her first report in four years.

I do not contest that the complaint reads as a dangerous-driving allegation — it is the rider's own words and my brief already states it — but agreeing that it is an allegation is not agreeing that it is true: SAFE-2 sends it to a person, and F1 shows a 10.5 km drive against a 10.6 km optimal route, i.e. nothing in the system record corroborates the manner of driving.

I do not dispute that F6 is in the record and is discourteous; but F6 is a post-trip written statement that ends by denying the allegation ('I drove normally'), it names no threat, no intimidation and no harassment, and a rude word is not the abuse SAFE-1 targets — the judge reads F6 and decides.

Accepted as far as it goes, and it cuts for the driver too: F5 confirms the chat record is complete and every message timestamped, so there is no G12 evidence gap and no missing rider message in which the rider raised any concern about the driving during the trip.

Agreed that the route data does not decide the safety question, but F1 and F2 are the only objective record of the drive and both point to an ordinary trip — 10.5 km / 15.9 min against a 10.6 km / 16.5 min estimate — so they at least refute the 'whole way' characterisation used in the complaint.

The rider's clean profile (F7) supports good faith and I do not contest it; it does not add any fact about the driving, and on the driver's side F8 (3.9 years, 4.78 rating, 705 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld) is at least as strong an indicator that this single occurrence, if it occurred, was an isolated one — so no account flag is warranted under RD-6.
